extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to os.system(), allowing arbitrary command execution (e.g., '127.0.0.1; rm -rf /').

User-controlled 'fragment' parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered as HTMLResponse. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to remote code execution and reflected XSS.

User-controlled 'packet_ref' query parameter is concatenated directly into a filesystem path using the '/' operator. An attacker can read arbitrary files via path traversal (e.g., '../../../etc/passwd').

User-controlled 'name' query parameter is used to construct a file path under BASE_EXPORT_DIR without sanitization, then request body bytes are written to that path. Allows writing arbitrary files via path traversal (e.g., overwriting system files via '../..').

User-controlled 'url' query parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(), allowing Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). An attacker can probe internal services, read cloud metadata endpoints, or access localhost services.

User-supplied JSON body is passed directly as a MongoDB query filter to find_one(). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g., {'$gt': '', '$where': '...'}) to bypass logic or execute arbitrary JavaScript.
User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without validation. An attacker can redirect users to arbitrary external URLs for phishing attacks.
The full request body and Authorization header value are logged at WARNING level via logger.warning(). This exposes authentication tokens and sensitive request data to log files.
